title: Debris and Waste Disposal
summary: Debris thrown, dropped or left behind hurts people below and starts fires. OSHA's disposal rules cover chutes, floor-hole debris, prompt cleanup and covered containers for flammable waste.
talking_points: When material is dropped more than 20 feet to a point outside the exterior walls of a building, use an enclosed chute of wood or an equivalent material (29 CFR 1926.252(a)).

When debris is dropped through holes in the floor without a chute, the drop area must be enclosed with barricades at least 42 inches high and set back at least 6 feet from the projected edge of the opening. Post signs warning of falling material at each level, and stop work below until the debris handling above is done (1926.252(b)).
Remove scrap lumber, waste and rubbish from the immediate work area as work progresses (1926.252(c)).
Any burning of waste must follow local fire regulations (1926.252(d)).
Keep solvent waste, oily rags and flammable liquids in fire-resistant covered containers until they are removed from the site (1926.252(e)).

Containers must be provided for the collection and separation of waste, trash, oily and used rags, and other refuse. Containers for garbage and for oily, flammable or hazardous waste, such as caustics, acids and harmful dusts, must have covers, and waste must be disposed of at frequent and regular intervals (1926.25(c)).
Remove combustible scrap and debris at regular intervals, and provide a safe way to do it (1926.25(b)).
Good practice: keep waste sorted into the right containers so hazardous waste never ends up in a general dumpster.
site_hazards_to_check: Material dropped more than 20 feet with no enclosed chute
Debris dropped through floor openings with no barricade or warning sign
People working below an active debris drop
Scrap and rubbish piling up in the work area
Oily rags and solvent waste in open or non-fire-resistant containers
Overflowing dumpsters and uncovered waste containers
discussion_questions: Where on this site do we drop debris from above, and how is the area below protected?
Where do oily rags and solvent waste go at the end of the day?
How often are waste containers emptied here?
